look.jp: この本を読んでください。
ここに名前を書いてください。
ちょっとまってください。

guesses.answer: てください asks someone to do; ないでください asks them not to.
てください asks for an action; をください asks for a thing.

guesses.text: a polite request for a favour
guesses.answer: てください is a plain request; てもらえませんか asks whether they would, which is gentler.

en.rule: **て-form + ください** asks someone to do something politely: 書いてください (please write).

rival.text: てください asks someone to do; ないでください asks them not to.

twists.jp: どうぞ、すわってください。
twists.ask: With どうぞ, is this an order?

choices.text: Yes: sit down, at once.
No: an invitation, please have a seat.

twists.why: With どうぞ, てください offers rather than orders: どうぞ入ってください, どうぞ食べてください.

twists.ask: No て-form here. What is asked for?

choices.text: A thing: that water, please.
An action: please drink that water.

twists.why: Noun + をください asks for a thing; て-form + ください asks someone to do something: 水を買ってください.

twists.jp: ここに入らないでください。
twists.ask: ないでください here. What is asked?

choices.text: Please come in here.
Please don't come in here.

twists.why: てください asks someone to do; ないでください asks them not to.

lines.jp: おおさかまで一まい、おねがいします。
はい、すこしまってください。

scene.note: てください asks for an action (まってください); をください asks for a thing.

cue.tr: That's thirteen thousand six hundred yen.

ask.task: You didn't catch it. Ask him to say it slowly.

choices.jp: すみません、ゆっくり言ってもいいですか。
すみません、ゆっくり言わないでください。
すみません、ゆっくり言ってください。

ask.why: You ask him to do something: the て-form with ください.

quiz.why: ください follows the て-form: つかう → つかって. つかったください puts it after the た-form, the past, and つかうください after the dictionary form.
quiz.jp: この電話をつかってください。
つめたい水をください。
quiz.tr: Please give me some cold water.
quiz.why: をください asks for a thing; てください asks for an action.
て-form + ください is a request made to the listener: it asks them to come again tomorrow. If the speaker were the one coming, it would be 来ます.
quiz.jp: あした、また来てください。

choices.text: The person spoken to.
Someone who is not in the conversation.
The speaker.

quiz.why: 休む ends in む, so the て-form is 休んで, with the voiced で. 休んて forgets the voicing, and 休って uses the rule of う, つ and る verbs.
quiz.jp: ここで、すこし休んでください。
quiz.tr: Please rest here for a while.

quiz.jp: あの新しい本をください。
quiz.tr: Please give me that new book.
quiz.why: をください asks for a thing; てください asks for an action.

quiz.ask: What do すみません and ちょっと do before 読んでください?
quiz.why: すみません and ちょっと are softeners put before a request: the ask is still 読んでください, but it sounds gentler. Here すみません is « excuse me », not an apology.
quiz.jp: すみません、ちょっとこのかんじを読んでください。
quiz.tr: Excuse me, could you read this kanji for me?

choices.text: They turn it into an apology: the speaker is sorry about something.
They make it stronger: the speaker insists.
They soften the request: « Excuse me, could you just… ».

quiz.why: 行く is the exception: its て-form is 行って, not 行いて. 行きて joins the ます-stem to て, which is not how the て-form is made.
quiz.jp: まず、北口へ行ってください。
quiz.tr: Please go to the north exit first.

look.jp: たなかさんは学生ですか。
おちゃかコーヒーを飲みますか。
look.tr: Will you drink tea or coffee?

guesses.answer: か asks for information you do not have; ね asks the listener to agree with what you both see.

guesses.text: turns a statement into a question; also 'or' between nouns
how about…? (a suggestion, or asking an opinion)
A or B (a choice between two)
guesses.answer: A single か asks a question; か… か… offers a choice between two whole options.

ka.rule: **か** at the end of a sentence turns it into a question. Between two nouns it means « or ».

rival.text: A single か asks a question; か… か… offers a choice between two whole options.

twists.jp: ペンかえんぴつで書いてください。
twists.tr: Please write with a pen or a pencil.
twists.ask: か sits between two nouns here. What does it mean?

choices.text: « and »: with a pen and a pencil
« or »: with a pen or a pencil

twists.why: Between two nouns, か means « or »: one or the other. At the end of a sentence, it asks.

twists.jp: この電車はとうきょうへ行きますね。
twists.tr: This train goes to Tokyo, doesn't it?
twists.ask: ね, not か. What is the speaker doing?

choices.text: Checking what they think they know: it goes to Tokyo, right?
Asking with no idea at all where it goes.

twists.why: か asks for what you do not know; ね checks what you think you both know.

lines.jp: すみません、これはおちゃですか。
いいえ、コーヒーです。おちゃもありますよ。
lines.tr: No, it's coffee. There is tea too.

scene.note: か at the end makes a question: you ask what you do not know.

ask.task: Ask him whether the tea is cold.

choices.jp: おちゃはつめたいですね。
おちゃはつめたいです。
おちゃはつめたいですか。

ask.why: You don't know whether it is cold: you ask, so か.

quiz.why: か between two nouns means « or »: ラーメンかカレー, one of the two. と would have both, and や would add « and so on ».
quiz.jp: ひるごはんは、ラーメンかカレーを食べます。
quiz.tr: For lunch I'll have ramen or curry.

quiz.why: か at the end makes the sentence a question, and 何時 is the missing piece, so the answer is a time, not yes or no. Without か it would be a statement.
quiz.jp: 友だちは、何時に来ますか。
quiz.tr: What time is my friend coming?

choices.text: It asks whether the friend will come or not.
It asks at what time the friend will come.
It says the friend will come at some time or other.

quiz.ask: At a crossing you ask a passer-by whether the station is on the left or on the right.
quiz.why: To offer a choice between two whole options, each one takes its own か: 左ですか、右ですか. 左か右です has か but states, it does not ask, and the third line leaves the second option without its か.

choices.jp: 駅は、左ですか、右ですか。

quiz.ask: You do not know the answer and want to find out. Which ending completes the sentence?
quiz.why: か asks for information you do not have: 来ますか. ね asks the listener to agree with what you both see, and よ tells the listener something they do not know.
quiz.jp: あした、先生は学校に来ますか。
quiz.tr: Will the teacher come to school tomorrow?

quiz.why: か between two nouns is « or », not a question: the sentence ends in ね, which asks the listener to agree. A real question would end in か: 雨かゆきですか.
quiz.jp: あしたは、雨かゆきですね。
quiz.tr: Tomorrow it will be rain or snow, won't it?

choices.text: Asking the listener whether it will be rain or snow.
Remarking that it will be rain or snow, and expecting the listener to agree.
Saying it will be both rain and snow at once.

look.jp: 今日は学校に行かない。
look.tr: I'm not going to school today.

look.jp: わたしはさかなを食べない。
ねる前にコーヒーは飲まない。
look.tr: I don't drink coffee before bed.

guesses.answer: ない is the plain negative; ません is the same negative, polite.
The ない-form alone says you do not; with でください it asks someone not to.

nai.rule: The **ない-form** is the plain negative: う-verbs take the あ-row + ない (行く→行かない, 買う→買わない), る-verbs drop る (食べない), する→しない, 来る→来ない (こない). ある becomes ない alone.
nai.structure: う-verb あ-row ・ る-verb stem + ない

structure_furigana.text: う-verb あ-row ・ る-verb stem + ない

rival.text: ない is the plain negative; ません is the same negative, polite.

twists.notion: Verbs in う: 買う → 買わない
twists.jp: パンは、あの店では買わない。
twists.tr: I don't buy bread at that shop.
twists.ask: In 買わない, where does the わ come from?

choices.text: 買う ends in う, and the あ-row sound of う is わ: 買わ + ない.
It is the sentence-ending わ, a softener added to 買う.

twists.why: A う-verb takes the あ-row sound before ない, and for う that sound is わ: 買う → 買わない, 会う → 会わない. Never 買あない.

twists.notion: Irregulars: する and 来る
twists.jp: あしたは、友だちがここにこない。
twists.tr: My friend isn't coming here tomorrow.
twists.ask: こない is the negative of which verb?

choices.text: 行く: こない means « don't go ».
来る: 来る → 来ない, read こない.

twists.why: The two irregular verbs: する → しない, and 来る → 来ない, read こない. Every other verb follows the rule.

twists.jp: つくえの上に本がない。
twists.tr: There is no book on the desk.
twists.ask: ない comes right after 本が, with no verb before it. What does the sentence say?

choices.text: I don't read the book on the desk.
There is no book on the desk.

twists.why: The plain negative of ある is just ない: 本がある, 本がない.

twists.jp: きのうは、ばんごはんを食べなかった。
twists.ask: 食べなかった. What does the sentence say?

choices.text: I won't eat dinner tomorrow.
I didn't eat dinner yesterday.

twists.why: After a verb, ない changes like an い-adjective: ない → なかった, the plain past negative.

twists.notion: After a noun: じゃない
twists.jp: これは、わたしのかさじゃない。
twists.ask: かさ is a noun, with no verb to negate. What does the sentence say?

choices.text: This isn't my umbrella.
I don't have an umbrella.

twists.why: After a noun the plain negative is じゃない (ではない), not ない alone: かさだ → かさじゃない. Alone, ない negates a verb, or ある.

twists.jp: あしたは、パーティーに行かない。
twists.tr: I'm not going to the party tomorrow.
twists.ask: You say this to your teacher. What is wrong?

choices.text: Nothing: ない is the polite negative.
It is too casual: to a teacher, the negative is 行きません.

twists.why: At the end of a sentence, ない is for friends and family. To a teacher or a stranger, the negative is ません: 行きません.

lines.tr: The train isn't coming, is it?

scene.note: Between friends, ない is the plain negative; with a clerk you would say ません.

ask.task: You don't feel like bread. Say no, the way you would to a friend.
ask.why: A friend gets the plain negative: 食べない. 食べません is for a clerk, and 食べないで asks the other person not to eat.

quiz.why: 買う ends in う, so it takes the あ-row sound わ before ない: 買わない. 買ない treats it as a る-verb, and 買わなかった is the past.
quiz.jp: わたしは新聞を買わない。

quiz.why: The negative is in the second half: わたしは食べない. The first half, おとうとは…食べる, is positive.
quiz.jp: おとうとはさかなを食べるが、わたしは食べない。
quiz.tr: My little brother eats fish, but I don't.

choices.text: The speaker does not; the brother does.
The brother does not; the speaker does.
Neither of them does.

quiz.ask: Your mother asks: しゅくだい、した？ You haven't done your homework. What do you answer?
quiz.why: She asks about something already past, so you answer in the past negative: しなかった. しない says you won't do it, and しませんでした is polite, for a teacher rather than your mother.

choices.jp: ううん、しませんでした。

quiz.why: A る-verb drops る before ない: 見る → 見ない. 見らない applies the う-verb rule, and 見るない keeps the る.
quiz.jp: ねる前は、テレビを見ない。
quiz.tr: Before bed, I don't watch TV.

quiz.ask: What does the sentence say about yesterday?
quiz.why: 出なかった is the past negative of 出る: it rained, so I didn't go out. The から gives the reason.
quiz.jp: きのうは雨だったから、うちから出なかった。
quiz.tr: It rained yesterday, so I didn't leave the house.

choices.text: It rained, but I went out anyway.
It rained, so I stayed at home.
It will rain tomorrow, so I won't go out.

quiz.ask: You open the fridge: there is no milk left. You tell your family.
quiz.why: There is none: ない is the plain negative of ある, that is がない. 飲まない says you don't drink it, and ありません is the polite version, too stiff at home.

choices.jp: ぎゅうにゅうがありません。
ぎゅうにゅうを飲まない。
